Ahora Moisés apacentaba las ovejas de Jetro su suegro, sacerdote de Madián; y llevó las ovejas atrás del desierto, y vino a la montaña de Dios, a Horeb –Éxodo 3:1.

El trasdós del desierto ha sido entendido desde hace tiempo como la escuela de Dios donde Él ha instruido a muchos de sus siervos, de entre los cuales Moisés es el principal. A la edad madura de 40 años, se hallaba …instruido en toda la sabiduría de los egipcios, y era poderoso en palabras y en hechos. Y cuando hubo cumplido cuarenta años, se le antojó visitar a sus hermanos los hijos de Israel –Hechos 7:22-23.

No tengo duda de que Dios puede, y efectivamente usa, a hombres de gran habilidad, capacidad y formación, pero el liderazgo espiritual requiere un ingrediente que no se deriva de hacer, alcanzar y lograr. La perdición del fanático suele ser poca confianza en Dios y demasiada confianza en la carne. Este orgullo e inquietud no se resuelven en un seminario ni normalmente se extinguen durante el celo vigilante. Para muchos de los siervos de Dios, se extraen del alma en el suelo de arenas desiertas. Esta aridez y terreno abandonado, que parece desprovisto de vida y fruto, es donde muchos siervos aprenden a poner su rostro en el polvo y ceder a lo que puede parecer inactividad, falta de fruto y rechazo.

La vida de Moisés puede dividirse en tres secciones. Pasó sus primeros cuarenta años aprendiendo la sabiduría de Egipto, los siguientes cuarenta como pastor en Madián, y los últimos cuarenta como pastor de Israel. Podemos imaginar que el primer tercio de su peregrinaje estuvo lleno de tremenda actividad, avance y logros. Sin duda le habían repetido que al nacer él …fue precioso a la vista, y criado en la casa de su padre tres meses –Hechos 7:20.

El milagroso rescate en el río por la hija de Faraón serviría para confirmar que estaba destinado a ser un instrumento de la divina orquestación de Dios. Como centro de atención nacional, es comprensible cómo este hombre que …era poderoso en palabras y en hechos –Hechos 7:22, rebosaba de confianza en sí mismo en su capacidad para cumplir el mandato de Dios.

En la economía de hoy, Moisés sería estimado como el candidato ideal para el liderazgo de la iglesia. Estaba cualificado en todo sentido. Se distinguía entre sus compatriotas en educación, y poseía dones naturales, financieros y espirituales por encima de lo común. Había emergido de la “Universidad” de Egipto como hombre poderoso en palabra y en obra y tenía una llamada evidente de Dios sobre su vida. Era un hombre conservador que eligió …más bien sufrir aflicción con el pueblo de Dios, que gozar de los placeres del pecado por un tiempo –Hebreos 11:25.

Aun así, en medio de todos sus excelentes credenciales aún era deficiente para la obra a la que Dios le había llamado. Y así, Dios lo condujo convenientemente a la tierra de Madián para inscribirlo en otra escuela, para que se alimentara de las hierbas amargas de la decepción y el rechazo, de la oscuridad y la soledad, y de sueños y anhelos no realizados. Mientras que su ambición anterior era alinearse voluntariamente con el pueblo de Dios, este capítulo de su vida se representó por compulsión.

Aprendemos del relato en Éxodo que el último tercio de su vida estuvo cargado de compleja implicación y gran ministerio. Aunque la salida de Egipto es una lectura emocionante y ofrece gran entendimiento, la mayoría de nosotros no puede identificarse honestamente con el poderoso Moisés y su dinámica coalición con Dios. Más bien, es la sección intermedia de 40 años, sin sucesos llamativos, en la que muchos de nosotros nos hallamos. Aunque solo hay unas pocas docenas de versículos que representan estas cuatro décadas de su vida, suponemos que fue una formación a fondo que inscribió inmensa paciencia, examen de alma y quizás un poco de frustración.

Para nosotros representa un período en que las arenas resecas del tiempo a nuestro alrededor parecen producir nada más fructífero que la revelación de nuestro corazón seco y costroso—marchito y desperdiciado por las consecuencias de nuestros fracasos y pecados pasados. Es en esos tiempos cuando podemos tener una caída en la fe, no porque culpemos a Dios por nuestras circunstancias, sino porque empezamos a ver nuestras vidas como fútiles, y que cada día es igual al anterior. Tal vez comencemos a caminar en un estupor sin visión—a través de una niebla de depresión espiritual—mientras tanteamos en busca de ánimo y un recordatorio de que Dios no nos ha olvidado. A veces incluso parece que nuestras oraciones chocan con el techo y rebotan, riéndose y mintiéndonos en burlona mueca de que nuestro uso en el Reino de Dios ha terminado. Durante tiempos prolongados de pruebas y escrutinio, podemos sentirnos abandonados. Incluso podemos imaginar que Dios se ha vuelto contra nosotros. Alzamos la vista al cielo y preguntamos: “¿Por qué, Señor?” Nunca experimentaremos el rechazo y el abandono hasta el extremo que el Señor Jesús sufrió, pero cuando los experimentamos en nuestro pequeño ámbito, parece que agotan toda nuestra fuerza y vigor espiritual. Pensamos… Si el Señor requiriera cuarenta años de esto de nosotros no quedaría tiempo en nuestras vidas para capitalizar lo que hemos aprendido. Pero el tiempo de Dios es perfecto. Así que nos conviene no preocuparnos tanto por la duración de nuestra instrucción, sino familiarizarnos a fondo con el mensaje de Madián. Mientras algunos reciben las amargas lecciones de Madián y se retiran para permanecer cínicos al margen, debemos sacudirnos el polvo del desierto y levantarnos con un entendimiento de…

El propósito de Dios

Dios tiene un propósito para cada detalle de nuestras vidas. Puede plantarnos en una posición difícil, para forjar en nosotros una nueva vocación. Fue en solitario en Madián donde Moisés aprendió de su propio orgullo, autoconfianza, falta de fe y la estupidez total en la que habían participado sus propias manos. Aquí en su Madián, estaba solo y sin embargo no estaba solo; numerosos otros santos se han unido a él allí. Los hijos de Jacob y la mujer de Potifar enviaron allí a otro siervo vibrante—José. La furia salvaje de un rey celoso envió allí a un joven arpista talentoso. Incluso un rey viejo y necio que se negó a ser enseñado se encontró en un desierto comiendo pasto como un buey hasta que renegó de su orgullo.

A lo largo de las páginas de la historia, incontables santos han comprendido que ‘cuanto más oscuro el valle, más aprendí a orar’. Si bien llegan al umbral del nuevo día cargados de exuberancia abundante, pronto son despojados en un cambio metamórfico y finalmente emergen con nada más que la vara de Dios en sus manos. Han desaparecido los días en que eran rápidos para hablar, rápidos para actuar y lentos para oír. En Madián, el discípulo aprende a cambiar su enfoque de “Haré grandes cosas para Dios” a “¿Qué quieres que haga?”

Y él, temblando y atónito, dijo: Señor, ¿qué quieres que haga? Y el Señor le dijo: Levántate y entra en la ciudad, y allí te dirán lo que debes hacer –Hechos 9:6. Los recién llegados a Madián tienen muchas respuestas, pero la mayoría de ellas implican una obra unipersonal con el yo como personaje principal. Los graduados salen en silencio y sobrios, pues han pasado por el arduo proceso de separar la carne del espíritu que se realizó mediante…

La purificación de Dios

El crisol es para la plata y el horno para el oro; mas Jehová prueba los corazones –Proverbios 17:3. Cuando Moisés pasó por las puertas de Madián, la primera escena que Dios puso delante de sus ojos fue una injusticia en un pozo. Ahora el sacerdote de Madián tenía siete hijas… –Éxodo 2:16, que estaban siendo apartadas por un grupo de pastores rudos. Pero Moisés había sido bien formado en toda la dimensión de la plutocracia egipcia, lo cual habría incluido todos los aspectos de la experiencia militar y las habilidades de liderazgo mundano. Por tanto, cuando intervino para ayudar a las pastoras desamparadas, habría sido bastante capaz de hacerlo. Estas hijas del sacerdote de Madián apreciaron la ayuda y se lo contaron a su padre que …Un egipcio nos libró de mano de los pastores, y además nos sacó agua suficiente y dio de beber al ganado –Éxodo 2:19. Al escuchar este relato, su padre, Reuel, quedó tan impresionado que le dio a Moisés una recepción, un trabajo y una esposa… todo en un versículo. –véase Éxodo 2:21.

…Sabéis que los que se estiman que gobiernan sobre las naciones se enseñorean de ellas; y sus grandes ejercen autoridad sobre ellas –Marcos 10:42. Si bien la búsqueda de justicia de Moisés pudo haber sido noble, su orientación era meramente gentil. Esto puede funcionar para establecer el orden en un gallinero, pero está destinado al fracaso al conducir al pueblo de Dios. Mas entre vosotros no será así; antes el que quiera hacerse grande entre vosotros será vuestro servidor: y el que de vosotros quiera ser el primero será siervo de todos –Marcos 10:43-44.

Esta doctrina era ajena a Egipto y también a Moisés. Muchos hombres buenos y talentosos pueden dirigir con éxito un negocio usando la autoridad gentil, pero rara vez funciona en su hogar, y es aún más inútil en una iglesia. Así, Dios movió a su vaso escogido de la realeza al proletariado (la clase trabajadora), casi de la noche a la mañana. Entonces se le dio un trabajo que era detestado por la gente que lo había formado—…porque todo pastor es abominación para los egipcios –Génesis 46:34. Este crisol no solo es para enseñarnos una lección muy necesaria, sino para guiarnos hacia…

La provisión de Dios

Guiará a los mansos en juicio, y enseñará a los mansos su senda –Salmo 25:9. Dios nunca nos abandonará en el trasdós del desierto; en cambio, Él ajusta las circunstancias de nuestra vida para traernos a su plenitud. Si resistimos la tentación de adoptar una actitud de ira, entonces Dios podrá enseñarnos sus caminos. Pero para Moisés, la situación se presentó de tal manera que la dirección divina de Dios fue lo último que sospecharía que estaba sucediendo.

¿Sucediendo…? Parecía que no sucedía nada. Las semanas se derritieron en meses, los meses en años y los años en décadas, todo el tiempo el dotado Moisés permaneció como un pastor de bajo rendimiento. Una de las cosas más difíciles con las que luchamos es la “espera”. Casi todo cristiano enfrentará un largo tiempo de tribulación y se nos dice: …No os maravilléis del fuego de la prueba que os ha sobrevenido, como si alguna cosa extraña os aconteciese –1 Pedro 4:12. Pero no debemos juzgar los medios de Dios por nuestro débil sentido, porque mientras tanto, la maravillosa obra de la espera nos prepara para…

El ascenso de Dios

38, 39, … 40 años. Ven, pues ahora, que yo te enviaré a Faraón, y sacarás de Egipto a mi pueblo, los hijos de Israel –Éxodo 3:10.

Quizás a Dios le guste el número 40, pero más probablemente fue el tiempo que le llevó a Moisés llegar al asiento de la resignación. Su autoestima se había extinguido por completo, y humildemente pregunta: …¿Quién soy yo, para que vaya a Faraón, y saque de Egipto a los hijos de Israel? –Éxodo 3:11.

Moisés no era menos cualificado que cuarenta años antes, pero su presunción se había evaporado al calor del sol del desierto. La experiencia adquirida en los ásperos pastos con las ovejas tercas lo ha llevado a comprender que esto será casi una hazaña imposible. Pero no hay llamado ordenado emitido independientemente de…

La promesa de Dios

…Ciertamente yo estaré contigo; y ésta será la señal para ti de que yo te he enviado: Cuando hubieres sacado al pueblo de Egipto, serviréis a Dios sobre esta montaña –Éxodo 3:12.

No es que Moisés hubiera alcanzado la perfección, porque encontramos a Moisés provocando la ira de Dios en el capítulo siguiente—Y se encendió la ira de Jehová contra Moisés… –Éxodo 4:14. Luego otra vez pronto es objeto directo en el camino de la espada de Dios—Y aconteció por el camino en la posada, que Jehová le salió al encuentro, y quiso matarle –Éxodo 4:24. Aun así, mientras su vaso todavía está hecho de barro, ha pasado por un fuego que lo ha preparado para el servicio del Señor, y para nosotros Dios no revocará sus promesas en el viento de nuestros caprichos. Así, el gran YO SOY EL QUE SOY –véase Éxodo 3:14, ha puesto sobre los hombros humanos la inmensa y eterna tarea de guiar a su pueblo. Pero este encargo no se ha de ejecutar sin…

El poder de Dios

¿Cuál fue la verdadera refinación del tiempo que Moisés pasó en el desierto? Observamos su precipitada disposición para blandir la espada antes de su llegada, pero al salir solo llevaba una vara en la mano. Con la espada había vencido a un ofensor egipcio, pero con la vara venció a las fuerzas enteras de Egipto. La vara de Dios hizo brotar el agua en el desierto. Fue la vara de Dios que, al ser levantada por manos débiles, aseguró la victoria sobre Amalec. ¿Qué es la vara de Dios? Antes de sus días en Madián, apenas sabía que existía. Cuarenta años después apenas existe una escena sin ella.

La vara es el poder de Dios para la salvación. Es la sabiduría de Dios, la verdad de Dios, el testimonio de Dios, pero más que todo ello es la corrección de Dios. Sin ella, el hombre no recibe ni percibe el amor de Dios; porque sin ella el hombre no está conectado con Dios. Porque a los que ama Dios, los reprende, y azota a todo hijo a quien recibe. Si soportáis la corrección, Dios os trata como a hijos; porque ¿qué hijo es aquel a quien el padre no corrige? Mas si estuviereis sin disciplina, de la cual todos son participantes, entonces sois bastardos, y no hijos –Hebreos 12:6-8.

Este mismo Moisés, que en un tiempo estuvo dispuesto a ejercer señorío (autoridad gentil) sobre el pueblo de Dios, ahora se encuentra suplicando a Dios y deteniendo su ira para que no los destruya. El pueblo que acusó a Moisés de sacarlos para matarlos e incluso en un momento estuvo dispuesto a apedrearlo está ahora en el centro de su corazón y afecto, aun cuando son la causa de su fracaso para entrar en la tierra prometida. Este es el amor de Cristo. Pero ¿dónde se aprende esto excepto bajo la vara de Dios, en el trasdós del desierto, en las mazmorras egipcias, en las cuevas de Adulam, en las estrecheces de Arabia y en la silenciosa soledad del segundo plano donde Dios ha ordenado que muchos de su pueblo vayan hasta que aprendan a …aprender de mí; porque soy manso y humilde de corazón: y hallaréis descanso para vuestras almas –Mateo 11:29. Seguramente es allí donde Moisés aseguró el carácter conocido por el erudito bíblico como el hombre más manso que anduvo sobre la faz de la tierra. Ciertamente no hay lugar más opuesto en la tierra para aprenderlo que en la escuela del sufrimiento.

Y así aquí habitaremos también, para que …podamos conocerle, y el poder de su resurrección, y la comunión de sus padecimientos, siendo hechos conformes a su muerte –Filipenses 3:10.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

Sekarang Musa menggembalakan kawanan domba Yitro, mertuanya, imam Madian; dan ia membawa kawanan itu ke belakang padang gurun, lalu datanglah ia ke gunung Allah, yaitu Horeb –Keluaran 3:1.

Belakang padang gurun sejak lama dipahami sebagai sekolah Allah tempat Ia mendidik banyak hamba-Nya, yang tertinggi di antaranya adalah Musa. Pada usia prima 40 tahun, ia mendapati dirinya …telah belajar segala kebijaksanaan orang Mesir, dan telah kuat akan perkataan dan perbuatan. Dan ketika ia genap berumur empat puluh tahun, timbullah dalam hatinya untuk mengunjungi saudara-saudaranya, orang-orang Israel –Kisah Para Rasul 7:22-23.

Saya tak ragu bahwa Allah dapat, dan memang memakai, orang-orang yang berbakat besar, berkapasitas, dan terlatih, tetapi kepemimpinan rohani memerlukan unsur yang tidak berasal dari melakukan, mencapai, dan meraih prestasi. Musibah kaum fanatik seringkali adalah terlalu sedikit percaya kepada Allah dan terlalu banyak percaya kepada daging. Kesombongan dan kegelisahan ini tidak ditangani di seminari maupun biasanya tidak dimusnahkan selama tugas yang teliti. Bagi banyak hamba Allah, hal itu dicabut dari jiwa di tanah berpasir tandus. Lahan kering dan ditinggalkan ini yang tampak kosong hidup dan kesuburan adalah tempat banyak hamba belajar menempelkan wajah mereka ke debu dan menyerah pada apa yang tampak sebagai ketidakaktifan, ketidakberbuah, dan penolakan.

Hidup Musa dapat dibagi menjadi tiga bagian. Ia menghabiskan empat puluh tahun pertama mempelajari kebijaksanaan Mesir, empat puluh tahun berikutnya sebagai gembala di Madian, dan empat puluh tahun terakhir sebagai gembala Israel. Kita dapat membayangkan bahwa sepertiga pertama dari peziarahannya dipenuhi aktivitas luar biasa, kemajuan, dan pencapaian. Tanpa diragukan lagi kepadanya telah diceritakan bahwa saat kelahirannya ia …sangat cantik rupa, dan diasuh di rumah ayahnya tiga bulan lamanya –Kisah Para Rasul 7:20.

Penyelamatan di sungai secara mujizat oleh putri Firaun akan mengonfirmasi bahwa ia ditakdirkan menjadi alat orchestrasi ilahi Allah. Sebagai pusat perhatian nasional, sangat dapat dimengerti bagaimana orang ini yang …kuat akan perkataan dan perbuatan –Kisah Para Rasul 7:22, penuh percaya diri akan kemampuannya melaksanakan kehendak Allah.

Dalam ekonomi masa kini, Musa akan dinilai sebagai kandidat ideal untuk kepemimpinan gereja. Ia dalam segala hal memenuhi syarat. Ia menonjol di atas bangsanya dalam pendidikan, dan ia memiliki karunia alamiah, finansial, dan rohani di atas rata‑rata. Ia muncul dari “Universitas” Mesir sebagai orang yang kuat dalam perkataan dan perbuatan dan ia memiliki panggilan yang nyata dari Allah atas hidupnya. Ia adalah orang konservatif yang memilih …lebih baik menderita sengsara bersama umat Allah daripada menikmati kenikmatan dosa untuk sementara waktu –Ibrani 11:25.

Namun, di tengah semua kredensialnya yang baik ia masih kekurangan untuk pekerjaan yang dipanggilnya. Maka, Allah dengan bijaksana membawanya ke tanah Madian untuk mendaftarkannya di sekolah lain agar ia memakan pahitnya kekecewaan dan penolakan, keterasingan dan kesepian, dan mimpi serta kerinduan yang tidak terpenuhi. Sementara sebelumnya ambisinya adalah dengan sukarela menyelaraskan dirinya dengan umat Allah, babak hidupnya ini dimainkan oleh paksaan.

Kita belajar dari catatan di Keluaran bahwa sepertiga terakhir hidupnya dipenuhi keterlibatan rumit dan pelayanan besar. Walau keluarnya dari Mesir adalah bacaan yang menggembirakan dan memberi wawasan besar, kebanyakan dari kita tidak dapat jujur berhubungan dengan Musa yang perkasa dan koalisi dinamisnya dengan Allah. Sebaliknya, adalah bagian tengah 40 tahun hidupnya yang tak berperistiwa itulah tempat banyak dari kita mendapati diri. Meski hanya ada beberapa puluh ayat yang mewakili empat dekade hidupnya ini, kita berasumsi bahwa itu adalah sekolah menyeluruh yang menanamkan kesabaran besar, pencarian jiwa, dan mungkin sedikit frustrasi.

Bagi kita, itu mewakili masa ketika pasir kering waktu di sekitar kita tampak tidak menghasilkan apa pun yang lebih berbuah selain menyingkap hati kita yang kering dan mengeras—menyusut dan terbuang oleh akibat kegagalan dan dosa-dosa masa lalu kita. Pada masa-masa inilah iman kita bisa goyah, bukan karena kita menyalahkan Allah atas keadaan kita, tetapi karena kita mungkin mulai melihat hidup kita sebagai sia‑sia, dan bahwa setiap hari sama seperti hari sebelumnya. Mungkin kita mulai berjalan tanpa visi—melalui kabut depresi rohani—sementara kita meraba untuk mendapatkan dorongan dan pengingat bahwa Allah belum melupakan kita. Kadang-kadang, tampak pula seolah-olah doa‑doa kita mengenai langit dan memantul kembali, menertawakan dan menipu kita dengan ejekan kelam bahwa kegunaan kita dalam Kerajaan Allah telah berakhir. Selama masa-masa panjang pencobaan dan ujian, kita dapat merasa ditinggalkan. Kita bahkan bisa membayangkan bahwa Allah telah berbalik melawan kita. Kita menengadah ke Surga dan bertanya, “Mengapa, Tuhan?” Kita tidak akan pernah mengalami penolakan dan ditinggalkan sampai sejauh yang Dialami oleh Tuhan Yesus, tetapi ketika kita mengalaminya dalam ranah remeh kita, hal itu tampak menguras seluruh kekuatan dan semangat rohani kita. Kita berpikir… Jika Tuhan menuntut empat puluh tahun ini dari kita, tidak akan ada waktu lagi dalam hidup kita untuk memanfaatkan apa yang telah kita pelajari. Tetapi waktu Allah sempurna. Oleh karena itu, semestinya kita tidak terlalu mempermasalahkan lamanya masa sekolah kita, melainkan menjadi benar‑benar mengenal pesan dari Madian. Sementara beberapa menerima pukulan pahit dari Madian dan mundur untuk berdiri sinis di pinggir lapangan, kita harus mengibas debu gurun dan bangkit dengan pengertian akan…

Tujuan Allah

Allah mempunyai tujuan untuk setiap detail hidup kita. Ia mungkin menanamkan kita dalam posisi yang sulit, untuk menempa dalam diri kita suatu panggilan baru. Di Madian sendirilah Musa belajar tentang kesombongan, percaya diri, kurang iman, dan kebodohan yang telah diperbuat oleh tangannya sendiri. Di sinilah di Madian, ia sendirian namun tidak sendiri; banyak orang kudus lain telah menyertainya di sana. Anak‑anak Yakub dan istri Potifar mengirim seorang hamba yang bersemangat ke sana—Yusuf. Amarah liar seorang raja yang cemburu mengirim seorang pemain kecapi muda yang berbakat ke sana. Bahkan seorang raja tua dan bodoh yang menolak diajar mendapati dirinya di padang gurun memakan rumput seperti lembu sampai ia mengaku kembali kesombongannya.

Sepanjang halaman sejarah, tak terhitung orang kudus menyadari bahwa ‘semakin gelap lembah, semakin aku belajar berdoa’. Ketika mereka tiba di ambang hari baru dengan penuh sorak gembira, mereka segera dilucuti dalam perubahan metamorfosis dan akhirnya muncul dengan tidak lain kecuali tongkat Allah di tangan mereka. Hilang sudah hari‑hari ketika mereka cepat berbicara, cepat bertindak, dan lambat mendengar. Di Madian, murid belajar mengalihkan fokusnya dari, “Aku akan melakukan hal‑hal besar bagi Allah” menjadi “Apa yang Kau kehendaki aku lakukan?”

Dan ia gemetar serta terkejut lalu berkata: Tuan, apa yang kehendaki-Mu supaya aku perbuat? Jawab Tuhan kepadanya: Bangunlah, pergi ke kota, maka akan diberitahukan kepadamu apa yang harus kauperbuat –Kisah Para Rasul 9:6. Pendatang baru di Madian memiliki banyak jawaban, tetapi kebanyakan melibatkan sandiwara satu babak dengan diri sendiri sebagai pemeran utama. Lulusan keluar dengan diam dan tenang, sebab mereka telah melalui proses berat memisahkan daging dari roh yang dikerjakan oleh…

Penyucian Allah

Ketel itu untuk perak, dan tungku itu untuk emas; tetapi TUHAN menguji hati –Amsal 17:3. Ketika Musa melewati gerbang Madian, adegan pertama yang Allah letakkan di hadapannya adalah suatu ketidakadilan di sebuah sumur. Sekarang imam Madian mempunyai tujuh anak perempuan… –Keluaran 2:16, yang diusir oleh rombongan penggembala kasar. Tetapi Musa sudah terlatih dalam segala dimensi plutokrasi Mesir, yang termasuk segala aspek keahlian militer dan keterampilan kepemimpinan duniawi. Jadi, ketika ia turun tangan menolong gembala‑gembala perempuan yang tak berdaya itu, ia tentu mampu melakukannya. Anak‑anak perempuan imam Madian menghargai bantuan itu sehingga mereka menceritakannya kepada ayah mereka bahwa …Seorang Mesir telah melepaskan kami dari tangan para gembala, bahkan ia menarik air secukupnya bagi kami dan memberi minum kawanan domba –Keluaran 2:19. Setelah mendengar cerita ini, ayah mereka, Reuel, begitu terkesan sehingga ia memberi Musa sebuah jamuan, sebuah pekerjaan, dan seorang istri… semua dalam satu ayat. –lihat Keluaran 2:21.

…Kamu tahu bahwa mereka yang dianggap memerintah atas bangsa‑bangsa sewenang‑wenang memerintah mereka; dan orang‑orang besar mereka berkuasa atas mereka –Markus 10:42. Walau perjuangan Musa untuk keadilan mungkin mulia, orientasinya hanya bersifat kebangsaan asing (Gentile). Ini mungkin berhasil untuk menetapkan urutan dalam kandang ayam, tetapi ditakdirkan gagal dalam memimpin umat Allah. Akan tetapi barangsiapa hendak menjadi besar di antara kamu, hendaklah ia menjadi pelayanmu: Dan barangsiapa di antara kamu hendak menjadi yang terdahulu, hendaklah ia menjadi hamba bagi semua –Markus 10:43-44.

Doktrin ini asing bagi Mesir dan bagi Musa juga. Banyak orang yang baik dan berbakat dapat berhasil mengoperasikan sebuah usaha dengan otoritas kebangsaan asing, tetapi itu jarang berhasil di rumah mereka, dan bahkan lebih sia‑sia di dalam gereja. Maka, Allah memindahkan bejana pilihan‑Nya dari kerajaan ke kaum proletariat (kelas pekerja), hampir dalam semalam. Ia kemudian diberi pekerjaan yang dibenci oleh orang‑orang yang telah melatihnya—…sebab tiap‑tiap gembala itu menghinakan orang Mesir –Kejadian 46:34. Ketel penyucian ini bukan sekadar untuk mengajarkan pelajaran yang sangat dibutuhkan, tetapi untuk membimbing kita ke dalam…

Penyelenggaraan Allah

Orang‑yang lemah hati akan Ia tunjukkan jalan dalam penghakiman: dan orang‑yang lemah hati akan Ia ajarkan jalan‑Nya –Mazmur 25:9. Allah tidak akan pernah meninggalkan kita di belakang padang gurun; sebaliknya, Ia menyesuaikan keadaan hidup kita untuk membawa kita ke dalam kepenuhan-Nya. Jika kita menahan godaan untuk mengadopsi sikap marah, maka Allah akan dapat mengajarkan kita jalan‑Nya. Tetapi bagi Musa, situasi memperlihatkan dirinya sedemikian rupa sehingga petunjuk ilahi Allah adalah hal terakhir yang akan ia curigai sedang terjadi.

Terjadi…? Tampaknya tidak ada yang terjadi. Minggu‑minggu mencair menjadi bulan, bulan menjadi tahun, dan tahun menjadi dekade, sementara Musa yang berbakat itu tetap menjadi gembala yang berkinerja rendah. Salah satu hal tersulit yang kita perjuangkan adalah “menunggu.” Hampir setiap orang Kristen akan menghadapi masa panjang kesengsaraan dan kita diberi tahu: …janganlah kamu heran akan nyala pepercobaan yang datang ke padamu, seakan‑akan sesuatu yang ganjil menimpa kamu –1 Petrus 4:12. Tetapi kita tidak boleh menilai cara‑cara Allah menurut rasa kita yang lemah, sebab sementara itu, pekerjaan menakjubkan dari menunggu mempersiapkan kita untuk…

Kenaikan Allah

38, 39, … 40 tahun. Karena itu, sekarang pergilah, sebab Aku akan mengutus engkau kepada Firaun, supaya engkau membawa umat-Ku, anak‑anak Israel, keluar dari Mesir –Keluaran 3:10.

Mungkin Allah menyukai angka 40, tetapi lebih mungkin, itulah waktu yang diperlukan bagi Musa untuk sampai pada kursi pengunduran diri. Harga dirinya telah sepenuhnya dipadamkan, dan ia dengan rendah hati bertanya: …Siapakah gerangan aku ini, sehingga aku pergi kepada Firaun dan membawa orang‑orang Israel keluar dari Mesir? –Keluaran 3:11.

Musa tidak kurang memenuhi syarat dibandingkan empat puluh tahun sebelumnya, tetapi prasangkanya telah menguap dalam teriknya matahari gurun. Pengalaman yang diperoleh di padang rumput yang keras bersama domba‑domba yang keras kepala telah membawanya pada pengertian bahwa ini akan menjadi usaha yang nyaris mustahil. Tetapi tidak ada panggilan yang ditetapkan yang dikeluarkan secara independen dari…

Janji Allah

…Sesungguhnya Aku akan menyertai engkau; dan ini akan menjadi tanda bagimu, bahwa Aku telah mengutus engkau: Apabila engkau telah membawa umat itu keluar dari Mesir, maka kamu akan beribadah kepada Allah di gunung ini –Keluaran 3:12.

Bukan bahwa Musa telah mencapai kesempurnaan, sebab kita dapati Musa memprovokasi murka Allah dalam pasal berikutnya—Dan murka TUHAN menyala terhadap Musa… –Keluaran 4:14. Lalu tak lama kemudian ia menjadi obyek langsung di jalan pedang Allah—Dan sesampainya mereka di rumah penginapan di jalan, TUHAN bertemu dengannya dan berusaha membunuh dia –Keluaran 4:24. Demikianlah, meskipun bejananya masih dari tanah liat, ia telah bertemu dengan pembakaran yang mempersiapkannya untuk pelayanan Tuhan, dan bagi kita Allah tidak akan mencabut janji‑Nya karena hembusan keinginan kita. Jadi, AKULAH AKU –lihat Keluaran 3:14, telah meletakkan di atas bahu manusia tugas yang amat besar dan kekal untuk memimpin umat‑Nya. Namun amanat ini tidak boleh dilaksanakan tanpa…

Kuasasa Allah

Apa penyucian sejati dari masa Musa di padang gurun? Kita memperhatikan kesediaannya yang gegabah untuk mengangkat pedang sebelum kedatangannya, tetapi ketika ia keluar, ia hanya memegang sebuah tongkat di tangannya. Dengan pedang ia telah mengalahkan seorang orang Mesir, tetapi dengan tongkat ia mengalahkan seluruh kekuatan Mesir. Tongkat Allah memunculkan air di padang gurun. Itulah tongkat Allah yang, ketika diangkat tinggi oleh tangan yang lemah mengamankan kemenangan atas Amalek. Apa itu tongkat Allah? Sebelum hari‑harinya di Madian, ia hampir tidak mengetahuinya. Empat puluh tahun kemudian hampir tidak ada adegan tanpa itu.

Tongkat itu adalah kuasa Allah membawa keselamatan. Itu adalah hikmat Allah, kebenaran Allah, kesaksian Allah, tetapi lebih dari semua itu adalah pengajaran Allah dengan tegas. Tanpanya, manusia tidak menerima maupun menyadari kasih Allah sebab tanpanya manusia tidak terhubung kepada Allah. Allah mengasihi semua orang yang Ia hukum; Ia memukul dan menegur setiap anak yang Ia terima. Jika kamu menanggung pengajaran, maka Allah memperlakukan kamu sebagai anak‑anak; sebab anak manakah yang tidak dipukul oleh bapanya? Tetapi jika kamu tiada mendapat didikan, yang semuanya memperoleh bagian dalam itu, maka kamu adalah anak haram dan bukan anak –Ibrani 12:6-8.

Musa yang sama ini, yang pada suatu ketika bersedia menggunakan kekuasaan (otoritas kebangsaan asing) atas umat Allah kini mendapati dirinya memohon kepada Allah dan menahan murka-Nya agar tidak menghancurkan mereka. Orang‑orang yang menuduh Musa membawa mereka keluar untuk membunuh mereka dan bahkan pada satu titik siap melempari dia dengan batu kini berada di pusat hati dan kasih sayangnya, meskipun mereka menjadi penyebab kegagalannya memasuki tanah perjanjian. Inilah kasih Kristus. Tetapi di manakah kasih ini dipelajari kecuali di bawah tongkat Allah, di belakang padang gurun, di penjara‑penjara Mesir, di gua‑gua Adulam, di kesusahan Arab, dan dalam kesunyian tempat cadangan di mana Allah telah menetapkan banyak umat‑Nya pergi sampai mereka belajar untuk …belajar dari pada-Ku; karena Aku lemah lembut dan rendah hati dalam hati: dan kamu akan mendapat ketenteraman bagi jiwamu –Matius 11:29. Pasti di sanalah Musa memperoleh watak yang dikenal oleh sarjana alkitabiah sebagai orang yang paling lemah lembut yang pernah berjalan di muka bumi. Pasti tidak ada tempat yang lebih bertentangan di bumi untuk mempelajarinya selain di sekolah penderitaan.

Dan di sinilah kita juga harus tinggal, supaya kita …dapat mengenal Dia dan kuasa kebangkitan-Nya dan persekutuan pada penderitaan‑Nya, sehingga kita menjadi serupa dengan kematian‑Nya –Filipi 3:10.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

现在摩西牧养他岳父米甸祭司叶忒罗的羊群；他把羊群赶到旷野的后边，来到神的山，就是何烈山。——出埃及记 3:1。

旷野的后边长期被理解为神的学堂，祂在那裡教训过祂的许多仆人，其中以摩西为首。四十岁壮年时，他发现自己…在埃及一切的学问上都受了教训，且有权势，言语和作为都显大能。既满了四十岁，就起意往他的弟兄那里去看他们的情形。——使徒行传 7:22-23。

我毫不怀疑神能够并且确实使用有大才能、能力和训练的人，但属灵的领导需要一种不是来自做事、成就与达成的成分。热心者的祸患常常是对神信心太少，对血肉信心太多。这种骄傲与不安在神学院里得不到处理，通常在谨慎服事中也不能根除。对许多神的仆人来说，这些成分是在荒凉的沙地上从心灵里被抽出来的。那片干旱被遗弃、看似无生命和无丰产的地，是许多仆人学会把脸贴在尘土里，顺服看起来像不作为、无果和被弃绝的地方。

摩西的生命可以分成三段。他用头四十年学习埃及的智慧，接下来的四十年在米甸做牧羊人，最后四十年作以色列的牧者。我们可以想象，他朝圣之路的前一段充满了极大的活动、晋升和成就。毫无疑问，人们早已向他重申他出世时…甚是俊美，且在他父家三个月被养活。——使徒行传 7:20。

法老女儿在河边的奇迹救援证实了他注定要成为神旨意工具的事实。作为一位受全国关注的中心人物，可以理解这位…言语和作为都显大能的⸺使徒行传 7:22男子，如何充满自信，相信自己能完成神的差遣。

在今日的环境中，摩西会被看作教会领导的理想候选人。他在各方面都合格：在教育上远胜同胞，并具备超常的自然、财务和属灵恩赐。他从埃及的“大学”出来，成为言语与作为上显大能的人，而且生命上有明显的神的呼召。他是个保守的人，宁可…与神的百姓一同受苦，不肯暫時享受罪的快樂。——希伯来书 11:25。

然而，在这一切良好资历之中，他仍不足以胜任神所召他的工作。于是，神便带他到米甸去，把他送进另一个学堂，让他吞下失望与被弃绝、默默无闻与孤独、未实现的梦想与渴望这等苦菜。在早先，他是出于自己的志向愿意与神的子民同列；但这一章人生却是被迫上演的。

我们从出埃及记的记载中得知，他生命的最后一段充满复杂的参与与重大的服事。虽然出埃及的出路读来惊心动魄并提供了深刻的见解，但我们中大多数人不能诚实地认同那位大能的摩西与他与神的动态同工。相反，许多人发现自己正处在他生命中那无大事的四十年中段。虽然代表这四十年的经文只有数十节，但我们假定那是彻底的训练，刻印了极大的忍耐、灵魂的探求，或许还有一点沮丧。

对我们来说，那段时期代表着周遭干渴的时光似乎结出不了比显明我们干瘪、结壳之心更有成果的东西——被以往失败与罪的后果所干瘪与消耗。就在这些时候，我们的信心可能会有滑坡，并非因为我们责怪神我们的处境，而是我们可能开始把生命看作徒然，每一天都和前一天一样。也许我们开始在无异象的迟钝中徘徊——在属灵沮丧的迷雾里挣扎，寻求鼓励与提醒，表明神没有忘记我们。有时，甚至感觉我们的祷告拍在天花板上弹回，嘲弄地笑着对我们说我们在神国中的用途已尽。在长久的试探和试炼中，我们会感到被弃；甚至会想象神转而反对我们。我们仰望天问：“主啊，为什么？”我们永远不会经历到主耶稣所受的被弃和被撇之程度，但当我们在自己狭小的领域经历这些时，似乎耗尽了我们一切属灵的力量与活力。我们想……如果主要我们经历这样的四十年，我们的人生就没有时间把所学转化为结果了。但神的时机是完美的。因此，我们不宜过于关心服事学堂的长短，而要彻底熟悉来自米甸的信息。当一些人领受了米甸的苦涩打击并退居讥讽的旁观者时，我们必须抖去旷野的尘土，明白地起来认识……

神的目的

神为我们生命的每一处细节都有目的。祂可能把我们安置在艰难的位置上，为要在我们里面锻造新的职分。正是在米甸，摩西认识到自己的骄傲、自信、信心的缺乏和自己手所参与的极大愚妄。在他的米甸里，他独自一人，但并非孤立无援；许多其他的圣徒也曾与他同在。雅各的儿子和波提乏的妻子把另一个充满活力的仆人送到那里——约瑟。忌妒的王的暴怒把一位多才的年轻弹琴者送到那里。甚至一位年老且愚昧、不肯受教的王也发现自己在旷野里吃草如牛，直到他悔改他的骄傲。

纵观历史的篇章，无数圣徒体会到“山谷越黑暗，我越学会祷告”。当他们满带丰盛的热情来到新的一天门槛时，很快便在变形的改变中被剥去一切，最后只手持神的杖出来。他们曾经快言快语、急于行动而迟于聆听的日子已不复存在。在米甸，学生学会把焦点从“我要为神做大事”转向“主啊，你要我做什么？”

他战兢惊恐，问主说：主阿，你要我作甚麼事？主說：起來，下到城裡去，必有人告訴你當作的事。——使徒行传 9:6。新到米甸的人有很多答案，但大多数都涉及一人独角戏，把自己当作主角。毕业生默然而庄重地走出来，因为他们历尽了那艰苦的过程，把肉体与灵分开，这过程是借着……

神的熬炼

银子虽在窑中被炼，金子在炉中被试，惟耶和华试验人心。——箴言 17:3。当摩西经过米甸的门口时，神摆在他眼前的第一幕是在井旁的不义。当时米甸的祭司有七个女儿…——出埃及记 2:16，正在被一群放荡的牧人赶走。但摩西在埃及接受的训练是全方位的埃及富豪制度训练，其中当然包括一切军事专长与世俗的领导技巧。因此，当他上前帮助这些无助的牧女时，他完全有能力这样做。米甸祭司的这些女儿感激摩西的帮助，便回去告诉她们的父亲说：…有一个埃及人救我们脱离牧人的手，也替我们打水，把羊喂了。——出埃及记 2:19。听了这个故事，他们的父亲流利勒（利乌）深受感动，就为摩西设摆筵宴，给他一个差事并把女儿给他作妻子……都写在一节经文里。——参见出埃及记 2:21。

你们知道，外邦人的治理主张在他们中间作主。并且他们的尊贵人在他们身上有权柄。——马可福音 10:42。虽然摩西为公义而奋勇可敬，但他的取向仅是外邦人的。这在鸡舍中建立等级秩序也许行得通，但在领导神的子民时注定要失败。只是你们中间为首的，必须作你们的用人；谁愿为首的，必作众人的仆人。——马可福音 10:43-44。

这种教义对埃及和摩西来说都是陌生的。许多良善有才的人可以用外邦式的权柄成功经营生意，但这在他们的家庭中很少奏效，在教会里更是徒劳。因此，神几乎在一夜之间把祂所拣选的器皿从贵族移到无产者（工人阶级）。后来他得了一个受训他的民众所厌恶的差事——…因为放羊的人在埃及人为可憎。——创世记 46:34。这熬炼的窑不仅是要教我们一个非常需要的功课，还是要引导我们进入……

神的供应

谦和的人必要以公平教训他，谦和的人必要指教他的道。——诗篇 25:9。神绝不会把我们弃置在旷野的后边；相反，祂为我们量身准备生命处境，使我们进入祂的丰满。若我们抵挡以愤怒为怀的诱惑，神就能够教导我们祂的道。但对摩西来说，情势呈现得让他最不怀疑的是没有发生神圣的指引。

发生……？似乎什么也没有发生。数周融为数月，数月为数年，数年为数十年，而那有恩赐的摩西仍旧是没能出众的牧羊人。我们极难应付的一件事就是“等候”。几乎每个基督徒都要面对长久的苦难，而我们被告知要…要以为不寻常，倒要以为有喜乐；因为你们是与基督一同受苦，叫你们到了将来得荣耀的时候，也可以欢喜快乐。——彼得前书 4:12。但我们不应以我们软弱的感官来判断神的方式，因为在此期间，等候的奇妙作为正在为我们预备……

神的提拔

三十八、三十九、……四十年。来 现在，所以我要差你去见法老，使你把我的百姓以色列人从埃及领出来。——出埃及记 3:10。

也许神钟意数字四十，但更可能的是，这是摩西走到放下自我的那个地点所需的时日。他的自尊已被彻底熄灭，他卑微地问：我是誰，竟能去见法老，将以色列人从埃及领出来呢？——出埃及记 3:11。

摩西的资格并不比四十年前差，但他的妄自尊大在旷野烈日之下已消散。他在粗犷的牧场与顽梗的羊群中所得的经历使他明白这是几乎不可能的壮举。但任何一个蒙召并不在于独立于……

神的应许

我却必与你同在；这就可作你得以差遣的证据。你既把百姓从埃及领出来，就要在这山事奉神。——出埃及记 3:12。

并不是说摩西已经达成完全，因为我们见到摩西在下一章就惹动耶和华发怒——耶和华向摩西发烈怒…——出埃及记 4:14。随后不久他又成为神刀剑所对准的对象——到了路上在客店的时候，耶和华遇见他，要杀他。——出埃及记 4:24。即便如此，虽然他的器皿仍是泥器，祂已经用火煅造他，使他为主的服事预备好，而且对我们而言，神不会因我们的任性而收回祂的应许。因此，那位自有永有者——参见出埃及记 3:14，把带领祂子民的伟大与永恒任务放在人类肩头上。但这项差遣不在没有……的情况下施行。

神的能力

摩西在旷野时光的真实磨练是什么？我们注意到他在到来之前轻率地愿意挥刀，但在离开时，他手中仅拿着杖。以刀曾使他胜了一个埃及人，但以杖他胜过了埃及的整个势力。神的杖在旷野使水涌出。正是神的杖，当软弱的手举起时，在亚玛力那里得了胜。什么是神的杖？在他到米甸之前，他几乎不知其存在。四十年后几乎不存在没有它的场景。

这杖就是拯救的神能。它是神的智慧，神的真理，神的见证，但更甚于这些的是神的管教。没有它，人就不接受也不察觉神的爱；没有它，人就与神没有连接。主所爱的，他必管教，又鞭打他所收的每一个儿子。你们若忍受管教，神待你们如同待儿子；父亲不管教儿子，便是私生子了。——希伯来书 12:6-8。

这同一个摩西，曾经愿意用外邦人的辖制（作王权）管轄神的子民，如今却为他们恳求，阻止神的怒气毁灭他们。那些曾指责摩西把他们带出去要杀他们、甚至一度要用石头打死他的人，如今成了他心中与情感的中心，尽管他们是他不能进入应许之地的原因。这就是基督的爱。但除非在神的杖下，在旷野的后边，在埃及的地牢中，在亞杜蘭的洞穴中，在阿拉伯的狭困中，与在被神命定让许多子民去的沉寂孤独中学到这一点，否则哪能学成呢，直到他们学会…学我的样式；因为我心里柔和谦卑，你们当负我的轭，学我的样式，就必得着心灵的安息。——马太福音 11:29。诚然，那正是摩西赢得那位圣经学者称作世上最温柔之人的品格之处。世上再没有比受苦的学堂更相反的地方来学这个了。

因此我们也当在此常存，好使我们…晓得他，并得知他复活的大能，并晓得与他同受苦的交通，使我们在生命的死上模成他的样式。——腓立比书 3:10。

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.
